candidates.changes: None. Retain Book::CreateSectionBreakOriginalResource/CreateNewSections, AnchorUpdates::GetIDLocations, UpdateAllAnchorsWithIDs, UpdateExternalAnchors, TextResource::SetText, and SaveToDisk.

candidates.name: Scoped relocation plan within existing updates
candidates.changes: Retain resource representation, GUI/cache routing, and save machinery. Add OriginTargetKey(original content URL, fragment), duplicate counts, and final-resource locations. Adapt Book orchestration, GetIDLocations interface, both anchor passes, and move notifications; replace id-only selection in these operations.
order: Before mutation, resolve affected hrefs against original document bases and index source targets. Reject ambiguous or unsupported resolution.
Plan splits and final paths; map unique source targets to resulting resources. Calculate hrefs relative to final referring documents.
Validate planned references and paths; prepare changed strings. Defer the early working-resource save until validation.
Apply resource changes and SetText updates, then existing SaveToDisk/book-save operations. Reopen validation remains an implementation acceptance check.
candidates.recovery: Preflight refusal reports the offending reference before writes. Retain original strings for in-session rollback. Interrupted multi-file saving still depends on existing recovery; no crash-atomic guarantee.
candidates.cost: Transient O(targets + affected links + edited text); no persistent IDs. Moderate maintenance for URL normalization, moves, and both update passes.

candidates.name: Scoped relocation with staged publication
candidates.changes: Reuse C1 resolution and resource model. Add staged copies, original snapshots, commit journal, and recovery coordinator; extend publication beyond SetText.
order: Capture source bindings and validate C1 mappings before edits.
Write and validate staged contents and metadata; persist original snapshots, then a prepared journal.
Publish the completed book through verified atomic replacement where supported.
Record completion, synchronize live resources, and remove obsolete recovery data.
candidates.recovery: Refuse ambiguity before staging. Recover interrupted publication from journal/snapshots. Verify replacement durability per storage backend; otherwise refuse an atomicity guarantee.
candidates.cost: Temporary persistent storage proportional to the staged book plus snapshots; extra I/O and substantial recovery/platform maintenance.

chosen_candidate.reason: Scoped target identity and rebasing directly address preservation. Persistent transaction infrastructure has no demonstrated necessity here. Selection is provisional without code inspection or execution.
chosen_candidate.global_reversal: An unchanged-code pass on all cases favors C0. Required crash recovery or demonstrated unrecoverable partial saving favors C2.

source_to_choice.section: EPUB33, 4.2.5 URLs in the OCF abstract container
source_to_choice.supported: Content URLs derive from container paths; XHTML URL parsing typically uses the referring document content URL. This supports document scope and relative-path recalculation after relocation.
source_to_choice.unsupported: No Sigil repair algorithm, fragment canonicalization details, duplicate-target selection, or transaction protocol is supplied. OriginTargetKey and planning are engineering extrapolations.

predictions.assumptions: Ordinary document base, unique fn, successful save, stated filenames; shared across candidates.

candidate_outputs.C0: Expected ch1 href ch1_1.xhtml#fn and tail containing FOOTNOTE_A. Existing hash locates fn in tail; GUI/cache and reopened files agree after successful saving. Interface-based prediction.
candidate_outputs.C1: Plan binds original fn to ch1_1.xhtml; ch1 keeps ref, tail keeps FOOTNOTE_A, href becomes ch1_1.xhtml#fn. UI and reopened book resolve A.
candidate_outputs.C2: Same final contents, binding, and UI as C1; staging/journal exist transiently.

predictions.failure: Each fails if saved/reopened ref resolves nowhere or elsewhere; C2 also fails if recovery loses both prior and completed states.
predictions.minimum_contrary_evidence: A C1 prototype failing this simple case suspends selection. C0 passing this case alone does not settle boundary handling.

predictions.assumptions: Move participates in reconciliation before save; no base element or unsupported URL encoding; shared across candidates.

candidate_outputs.C0: Underdetermined: self may retain ch1.xhtml#fn, or repairs may retain pre-move filenames; toc A may be stale. Origin qualification suggests toc B remains ch2.xhtml#fn. GUI and persisted state can agree while links fail; cross-chapter hash contamination is unproven.
candidate_outputs.C1: Plan keeps A/B distinct. ch1 self and toc A become parts/ch1_tail.xhtml#fn; toc B stays ch2.xhtml#fn. Tail contains FOOTNOTE_A; ch2 retains FOOTNOTE_B. UI and reopened files preserve bindings.
candidate_outputs.C2: Same final objects, references, contents, and UI as C1; staged publication adds recovery metadata.

predictions.failure: Each fails if A reaches B, B reaches A, or a reopened reference is stale. C1/C2 additionally fail if moves bypass planning.
predictions.minimum_contrary_evidence: A baseline trace correctly handling qualified self-links, relocation, and scope removes the main justification for C1, conditional on SG-X success.

predictions.assumptions: Duplicate fn in one original document; no trusted target choice; shared across candidates.

candidate_outputs.C0: An id-keyed hash cannot represent both targets; absent another check, one location wins and ref silently follows FIRST or SECOND. Exact winner, file serialization, and UI warning are unknown.
candidate_outputs.C1: Duplicate-count objects expose ambiguity; preflight refuses. Original file and GUI remain unsplit; no target is guessed.
candidate_outputs.C2: Same refusal and unchanged contents/UI as C1; no staging or journal writes occur.

predictions.failure: C0 fails if it silently chooses. C1/C2 fail if they claim preservation from an untrusted choice. Unchanged bytes/digests identify content, not intended target identity.
predictions.minimum_contrary_evidence: Trusted provenance identifying the intended element permits binding and splitting. Existing baseline refusal plus SG-N/SG-E success would favor C0.
